caseStudy.context: Algérie Télécom's Information Systems Division ran projects with no centralized tool: fragmented tracking, scattered information, no cross-project visibility. The need: a single internal project management platform, designed with DSI supervisors.
caseStudy.role: Full Stack developer — requirements analysis, design, back-end (Laravel) and front-end (Vue.js) development, functional validation with the DSI.
constraints: Corporate environment: every deliverable validated by DSI supervisors
Dense business database: 26 interconnected tables (projects, tasks, users, audits)
Strict role-based access control (RBAC) across 42 functional screens
Calendar, Gantt chart and notifications within one coherent UX
approach: Requirements workshops with the DSI → UML modeling, then a 26-table database schema
Laravel MVC architecture: clean business API, strict separation of concerns
Component-based Vue.js front end, state managed per module
RBAC implemented at the authorization layer, tested screen by screen
caseStudy.outcome: A 42-screen platform adopted by the Information Systems Division: project tracking, planning (calendar + Gantt), full audit log and notifications — delivered and validated as the final year project.
